bullets: Risk is a systems property that lives in the couplings, not the components — a foundational insight that redefines how teams approach failure and resilience.
The most dangerous risks are slow, correlated, and predictable yet routinely discounted — naming them is the first step toward managing them effectively.
Systems thinking and risk management are not separate disciplines but one discipline expressed in two vocabularies — their convergence enables deeper insight into complex failures.
Teams using IPCC have repeatedly rebuilt solutions from scratch because they ignored the couplings — a sign that systems awareness is not optional but essential.
Reliability is not a component-level attribute but a property of interactions — trade-offs around reliability cross-cut every system design decision.
Framing matters because it reveals the hidden trade-offs embedded in any risk assessment — the right question determines the outcome.
Measuring the system directly confirms that risk emerges from couplings, not parts — this empirical validation shifts the focus from isolated failures to systemic behavior.
Try one idea from the conversation for two weeks; the rest is iteration — practical adoption begins with small, sustained experiments.
